intro: Google Lens is built into desktop Chrome on Mac, so there is no separate app to download. Open the More menu (the three dots at the top right), choose Search this tab with Google Lens, then select or drag over any part of the page.
tldr: Open More (the three dots, top right) and choose Search this tab with Google Lens.
Or right-click the page or an image and pick the Lens option from the menu.
Lens needs Chrome on macOS 13 Ventura or later and Google as your default search engine.
Press Esc to close the side panel. Google says a screenshot and page data go to Google when you search page content.

blocks.text: Google Lens is not a separate Mac app. It sits inside desktop Chrome, so you use it from the browser you already have open. Google's Chrome features page says Lens is built in and needs no setup when Chrome is your default browser. The feature is easy to miss because it lives in menus you may never open. This guide shows each route in, from the More menu to the right-click menu, and what to do once the results appear.
Check your Chrome and macOS versions first

Chrome on Mac needs macOS 13 Ventura or later, according to Google's update help page. To see your Chrome version, click More at the top right, go to Help, and choose About Google Chrome. The page checks for updates as it opens. If an update is ready, click Relaunch. Automatic updates only work when Chrome is installed in the Applications folder.

Wikipedia lists 157.0.8103.39 as the stable build, released 3 November 2026. I could not confirm that number against Google's own release notes, so treat it as a reference only. Your build should match the current stable release when you read this page.
Where to find Lens in Chrome on Mac

There are four ways in. Each one starts a Lens search, but they fit different jobs. Use the More menu when you want to search the page or a part of it. Use the right-click menu when you are already pointing at a picture. Use the address bar when you want to ask a question about the page. The table lists all four routes.

Right-click the page > Search this tab with Google Lens

Right-click the image > Search this image with Google Lens
Click the address bar > Ask Google about this page
blocks.caption: The four routes into Lens in desktop Chrome, from Google's help and features pages.

blocks.text: When Lens opens, a side panel appears. The results stay in that panel, not in a pop-up. Google's help page says you can type a question into the search box in the panel. You can also click or highlight text, or select and drag over any area, to search that part. Results open in a new tab when you select one. Press Esc to close the panel.
Search part of a page instead of the whole thing

Most pages hold more than one thing worth searching. A recipe page can have a photo, a list of ingredients and a link to a product. Lens can read each one, but you have to point it at the right part. Drag a box around the photo to search the photo alone. Highlight one line of text to search those words. A narrow selection makes the results easier to read, so start small and widen the box only if the first results miss.

blocks.title: Start small
blocks.text: Drag a tight box first. If the results miss the point, select a wider area and search again.
Right-click an image on a Mac

Right-clicking an image is the fastest route when the picture is the thing you care about. On a Mac, right-click the image or Control-click it. Choose Search this image with Google Lens. Google's features page uses that wording. Some third-party guides show Search Image with Google Lens instead, and older guides may differ again. Look for the Lens words rather than an exact match. Chrome opens the side panel and runs the search on that image.
Ask a follow-up or start from the address bar

The address bar route is the quietest. Click the address bar, then choose Ask Google about this page. Chrome's help page links that route to AI Mode. Inside the side panel, the Ask a follow up bar near the bottom also opens AI Mode. Use it when the first answer is close but not quite right. Your AI Mode history is under AI Mode, then View your AI Mode history.
Limits of Lens on the Mac

Desktop Lens has no live camera mode. You cannot point the Mac's camera at a product and expect results in real time. The workaround is plain. Take the photo on another device, move it to your Mac, and upload it to Google Images. iGeeks Blog describes this route for Mac users. Desktop Lens is built for things already on your screen, such as a page, a chart or a saved picture.

items: No live camera mode on desktop. Upload a photo from another device instead.
Google must be your default search engine, according to Chrome Help.
Google's help page gives no Chrome version or sign-in requirement for Lens.
Google's Chrome features page does not mention macOS at all.

blocks.text: What Google receives when you search with Lens

Google's help page says selected content goes to Google Search. When you search page content, a screenshot and page data go to Google as well. Google says it does not use the page or the image for training. It also says it keeps no data beyond temporary processing storage. You can manage the activity in My Google Activity. On a shared Mac, you may also want to clear your browsing data in Chrome.

The numbers explain why Lens sits in Chrome. Google's VP of Global Advertising said at a March 2026 briefing that Lens handles more than 25 billion visual searches per month. That briefing also put 20% of those searches at commercial intent. The Chrome homepage says Chrome gets a new update every four weeks. Labels can shift between releases, so check your version before you hunt for a menu item that is not where this guide says.
Mistakes people make with Lens in Chrome

items: Looking for a separate Lens app. There is none. The feature runs inside Chrome.
Skipping the default search engine setting. Google's help page treats it as a requirement.
Searching the whole page when one part matters. A tight box usually gives a cleaner answer.
Forgetting that the side panel stays open. Press Esc or choose Close when you finish.
Expecting live camera results on the desktop. Upload a photo from another device instead.

blocks.text: Where to go next

If you share this Mac, clear your browsing data before you hand it over. The steps are in [How to clear browsing data in Chrome on Mac](/how-to/clear-browsing-data-in-chrome). If Chrome is not your default browser yet, read [how to set Chrome as your default browser on Mac](/how-to/set-chrome-as-your-default-browser-in-chrome) first. Google's features page ties the built-in setup to Chrome being your default browser, so that step matters here.

faq.question: Is there a Google Lens app for Mac?
faq.answer: Not a separate one. Google's Chrome features page says Lens is built into Chrome. On a Mac, you start it from the Chrome window, through the More menu, the right-click menu or the address bar.

faq.question: Do I need Google as my default search engine?
faq.answer: Yes, according to Google's Chrome Help page, which says to set Google as your default search engine. Change it in Chrome settings, in the search engine section.

faq.question: Which macOS version do I need for Chrome on Mac?
faq.answer: macOS 13 Ventura or later. Google's update help page gives that requirement for Chrome on Mac. Google's Lens page does not mention macOS, so the requirement comes from the Chrome update page.

faq.question: Can Lens use the camera on my Mac?
faq.answer: Not in real time. Desktop Lens has no live camera mode. Take a photo on another device, move it to your Mac, and upload it to Google Images.

faq.question: Does Google keep what I search with Lens?
faq.answer: Google says a screenshot and page data go to Google when you search page content. It also says it keeps no data beyond temporary processing storage. You can manage the activity in My Google Activity.

faq.question: Why does the menu wording differ from this guide?
faq.answer: Google's Chrome homepage says Chrome gets a new update every four weeks. Third-party guides also use older labels. Check your version under More, then Help, then About Google Chrome.

faq.question: Can I use Lens in Safari on Mac?
faq.answer: This guide covers Chrome only. The sources used here do not cover Lens in Safari, so check Google's own support pages before you assume it works there.

faq.question: Where do I find past Lens searches?
faq.answer: Under AI Mode, choose View your AI Mode history. Your wider Google activity is managed in My Google Activity.

steps.name: Update Chrome on your Mac
steps.text: Open Chrome and click More at the top right. Go to Help, then About Google Chrome. Chrome checks for updates when the page opens. If an update is ready, click Relaunch.
steps.tip: Chrome on Mac needs macOS 13 Ventura or later. Automatic updates need Chrome in the Applications folder.

steps.name: Set Google as your default search engine
steps.text: Lens needs Google as the default search engine. Open Chrome settings, find the search engine section, and choose Google. The label can change between releases, so use the settings search box and type search engine.
steps.tip: Google's help page marks this setting as a requirement for Lens.

steps.name: Open the page you want to search
steps.text: Go to the page in Chrome. Scroll to the part you care about first, so it is on screen when you start the search.

steps.name: Open Lens from the More menu
steps.text: Click More, the three dots at the top right of the Chrome window. Choose Search this tab with Google Lens. A side panel opens next to the page.
menuPath: Search this tab with Google Lens
steps.tip: You can also right-click the page and choose the same item.

steps.name: Select the area to search
steps.text: Click or highlight text, or select and drag a box over an image or any part of the page. Lens searches the selection you made.

steps.name: Search an image from the right-click menu
steps.text: Right-click the image, or Control-click it. Choose Search this image with Google Lens. The result appears in the same side panel.
menuPath: Search this image with Google Lens
steps.tip: Some guides use the wording Search Image with Google Lens. Look for the Lens words.

steps.name: Ask a follow-up question
steps.text: Type a question in the search box in the panel, or use the Ask a follow up bar near the bottom. That bar opens AI Mode, so the answer can go further than the first result.
steps.tip: Your AI Mode history is under AI Mode, then View your AI Mode history.

steps.name: Start from the address bar
steps.text: Click the address bar at the top of Chrome, then choose Ask Google about this page. This route also leads into AI Mode.

steps.name: Close the side panel
steps.text: Press Esc, click the live page area, or choose Close in the side panel. Any of the three closes Lens and returns you to the page.
steps.tip: Esc is the only keyboard key Google's help page mentions for Lens.

steps.name: Pin Lens to the toolbar
steps.text: Google's help page says you can pin Search this tab with Google Lens to the toolbar. The page does not list the exact clicks, so look for a pin option on that menu item in your version of Chrome.
menuPath: Search this tab with Google Lens
steps.tip: A pinned item saves you opening the More menu each time you use Lens.

shortcuts.action: Open the right-click menu on an image (Mac)

troubleshooting.problem: The Lens option is missing from the More menu
troubleshooting.fix: Confirm Google is your default search engine in Chrome settings. Then check More, Help, About Google Chrome, relaunch if an update is waiting, and confirm macOS 13 Ventura or later. Google's help page lists no other fixes.

troubleshooting.problem: Google Images says the URL doesn't refer to an image, or the image is not publicly accessible
troubleshooting.fix: This error comes from the Google Images upload flow, not the Chrome side panel. Control-click the image, choose Copy Image Address, then paste it into the Paste image link field. iGeeks Blog describes this fix.

troubleshooting.problem: The side panel will not close
troubleshooting.fix: Press Esc, click the live page area, or choose Close in the side panel. Google's help page lists those three ways.

troubleshooting.problem: The results miss the part I selected
troubleshooting.fix: Select a narrower area and search again. For a question about the whole page, use the address bar route instead.

troubleshooting.problem: I need a result from an earlier Lens search
troubleshooting.fix: Open AI Mode, then choose View your AI Mode history. Google's activity controls are in My Google Activity.
